tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.summary: Identify which two atoms are isotopes from proton and neutron numbers.
Find x in a hydrated cobalt chloride formula from masses before and after heating.
Explain why the second electron affinity of oxygen is positive in a Born-Haber cycle.
units.difficulty_basis: conceptual understanding of electron affinity sign

units.summary: Calculate the volume of barium hydroxide needed to neutralise a given volume of hydrochloric acid.
Determine the rate of reaction at 30 s from a gas volume against time graph.
Calculate the C-H bond enthalpy from a given enthalpy of reaction and other bond enthalpies.
Choose the explanation for the rising boiling points of hydrogen halides.
Calculate the percentage uncertainty of a titre from two burette readings.
Deduce the rate equation from a two-step mechanism with a slow first step.
Select the positive electrode half-equation for an alkaline hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell.
units.difficulty_basis: needs fuel cell half-equation in alkaline conditions

units.summary: Identify the strongest reducing agent from two electrode potentials.
Calculate half-life from the rate constant of a first order reaction.
units.difficulty_basis: uses t half equals ln2 over k

units.summary: Choose a suitable indicator for titrating a weak acid with a strong base.
units.difficulty_basis: requires titration curve and indicator range reasoning

units.summary: Judge three statements about barium in Group 2 covering electron configuration, reactivity and ionisation energy.
Judge three statements about chromium complex ions covering oxidation state, colour and coordination number.
units.difficulty_basis: three statements need recall of complexes

units.label: 16(a)(i)
units.summary: Complete a graph of melting points for P, S, Cl and Ar in Period 3.
units.difficulty_basis: needs structure-based ordering of molecular melting points

units.label: 16(a)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why silicon has a higher melting point than aluminium using structure and bonding.

units.label: 16(b)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for the first ionisation energy of sulfur with state symbols.

units.label: 16(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why the first ionisation energy of sulfur is lower than that of phosphorus.

units.label: 16(c)
units.summary: State observations and ionic equations for bromine water with iodide and chloride ions.
units.difficulty_basis: recall of halogen displacement with equation

units.label: 16(d)
units.summary: Explain with dot-and-cross diagrams the different shapes and bond angles of SiH4, PH3 and H2S.

units.label: 17(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain why the standard enthalpy of formation of iron is zero.

units.label: 17(a)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy change of the iron(III) oxide reduction from formation enthalpies.

units.label: 17(a)(iii)
units.summary: Explain why gaseous carbon dioxide has greater entropy than solid iron(III) oxide.

units.label: 17(a)(iv)
units.summary: Calculate the standard entropy of iron from the entropy change and other entropies.

units.label: 17(b)
units.summary: Show a reaction is not feasible at 100 C and calculate the minimum feasible temperature using Gibbs energy.

units.label: 17(c)(i)
units.summary: Explain why Kp has no units for the steam and carbon monoxide equilibrium.

units.label: 17(c)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the equilibrium partial pressures of H2O and CO from Kp and partial pressures.

units.label: 17(c)(iii)
units.summary: Explain whether a larger Kp means a higher or lower temperature for an exothermic reaction.
units.difficulty_basis: links Kp change to enthalpy sign

units.label: 18(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain why platinum is a heterogeneous catalyst.

units.label: 18(a)(ii)
units.summary: Explain with a Boltzmann sketch how a catalyst increases reaction rate.

units.label: 18(a)(iii)
units.summary: Explain how catalysts benefit the environment.

units.label: 18(b)
units.summary: Determine orders, the rate equation and rate constant with units from initial rates data.
units.difficulty_basis: multi-part with units for third order

units.label: 18(c)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the missing value of ln k in a table.

units.label: 18(c)(ii)
units.summary: Plot ln k against 1/T, identify the anomaly and calculate activation energy from the gradient.
units.difficulty_basis: graph plotting plus gradient and unit conversion

units.label: 19(a)
units.summary: Calculate the pH of a strong monobasic acid.

units.label: 19(b)(i)
units.summary: Predict and explain whether a weak acid has higher pH than a strong acid of same concentration.

units.label: 19(b)(ii)
units.summary: Define disproportionation and show it with oxidation numbers for nitrous acid.
units.difficulty_basis: applies oxidation numbers to unfamiliar reaction

units.label: 19(c)
units.summary: Calculate mass of sodium propanoate for a buffer of given pH and explain action on adding alkali.

units.label: 20(a)(i)
units.summary: Draw a labelled cell diagram with conditions to measure the standard cell potential for two redox systems.
units.difficulty_basis: recall of cell set-up with Pt electrode

units.label: 20(a)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the standard cell potential from two electrode potentials.

units.label: 20(b)
units.summary: Explain a two-stage reduction by cobalt using electrode potentials and equilibrium shifts with equations.
units.difficulty_basis: unfamiliar vanadium system with integrated reasoning

units.label: 21(a)(i)
units.summary: Give the electron configurations of an Fe atom and a Cu2+ ion.

units.label: 21(a)(ii)
units.summary: Describe observations on adding sodium hydroxide to iron(II) sulfate and copper(II) sulfate.

units.label: 21(b)(i)
units.summary: Define a monodentate ligand.

units.label: 21(b)(ii)
units.summary: Determine an empirical formula from percentage composition then deduce ligand number and coordination number.
units.difficulty_basis: multi-step calculation in unfamiliar complex context

units.label: 21(c)
units.summary: Draw the other stereoisomer of a complex and name the type of stereoisomerism.
units.difficulty_basis: requires drawing a geometric isomer of a bidentate complex

units.label: 21(d)(i)
units.summary: Calculate percentage by mass of copper sulfate in a mixture from an iodine-thiosulfate titration.

units.label: 21(d)(ii)
units.summary: Suggest why the titre rises when some iron(II) is oxidised to iron(III).
units.difficulty_basis: unfamiliar reasoning about iron(III) oxidising iodide
